intro.title: Build typed visitor pattern
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple, typed visitor pattern to process different shapes like circles and squares. You'll learn how to use TypeScript interfaces and classes to define a set of operations that can be applied to various object structures without modifying those objects. The main technologies involved are TypeScript's type system, interfaces for visitor contracts, and concrete visitor implementations. This pattern helps keep your code extensible and organized when adding new operations.
intro.usecase: The visitor pattern is essential in TypeScript applications that need to process complex object structures with different behaviors. You'll see this in document editors like VS Code that apply formatting operations to various AST nodes, or in e-commerce platforms that calculate different taxes and discounts for diverse product categories. It's also used in UI component libraries where components need to accept different rendering strategies, and in data visualization dashboards that apply distinct processing logic to various chart types while maintaining type safety.
